title: How RAG Works: Retrieve, Then Generate
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation looks up relevant passages from your own data and places them in the prompt, so the model answers from evidence instead of memory. Its accuracy factors into two numbers you can measure separately: did retrieval find the evidence, and did the model use it faithfully.
objectives: Explain which problems retrieval solves (stale knowledge, private data, citations) and which it does not
Draw the offline indexing path and the online query path of a RAG system and name each component
Use P(correct) ≈ P(retrieved) × P(faithful | retrieved) to decide which half of a system to improve
Compute the token cost and latency of a RAG request from k, chunk size and prices
Choose between RAG, long-context stuffing and fine-tuning for a given use case
prerequisites: You should know what tokens and context windows are ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization), [Context Windows and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache)) and why models hallucinate ([Hallucination and the Limits of Next-Token Prediction](/learn/model-foundations/limits)). Embeddings as vectors ([Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings)) help but are revisited in the next lesson.
